prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a burst pipe in winter. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a burst pipe is reported in winter, check whether the heating was left on low or the property was emptied for a spell, because the pattern of expectations."},{"type":"fact","content":"When radiators, boilers or hot-water cylinders are mentioned, I should separate escape of water from the pipework from any heating failure, because the cause affects both coverage checks and repair planning."},{"type":"observation","content":"When damage is mostly to floors and lower walls, I should look for signs that the leak tracked along pipes or under
